evidence: Ingested data/training_data.csv (800 rows) into Hopsworks as feature group 'leakage_train' v1 and inspected the platform-computed descriptive statistics (hops fg stats). All of f1-f5 are well-behaved ~N(0,1): quartiles roughly symmetric about 0 (Q25/Q50/Q75 in [-0.71,-0.57]/[0.01,0.14]/[0.62,0.85]), mean ~0, stddev ~1.0. f6 is the only bimodal feature: Q25=-0.055, Q50=0.110, Q75=2.399, min=-0.406, max=2.843, mean=0.839, stddev=1.186. The distribution is two clusters (a low cluster near 0 and a high cluster near ~2.4); the jump occurs between the 50th and 75th percentile, so ~66% of rows sit in the low cluster and ~34% in the high cluster. That 33.9% high-cluster mass matches the positive-label rate exactly (label mean = 0.33875). Inspecting raw rows confirms f6 deterministically tracks the outcome (f6 ~ 2.3-2.5 when label=1, ~0 when label=0, plus small noise) — i.e. f6 was computed from post-outcome data and leaks the label. Note: per-label GROUP BY via 'hops sql' was unavailable because the offline FG table is neither a Hudi nor Iceberg table and no hive/delta Trino catalog is exposed on this cluster (catalogs: hudi, iceberg, tpcds, tpch), so the conclusion rests on the platform-computed feature statistics plus the bimodal-cluster/positive-rate match.
